correctness.rationale: For every independent base face σ, the colored augmented chain module is ⊗_{i∈σ}Q^n, with boundary applying color augmentations. The canonical S_n-invariant splitting Q^n=Q u_i⊕U_i divides the full chain into direct subcomplexes labeled by independent T⊆σ. Deleting positions in T vanishes and other deletions give, up to the explicit Koszul sign, the augmented link of T, shifted by |T|. The complement P_m\N[T] is a disjoint union of paths, whose independence complexes have one sphere when each block length is 0 or 2 mod3, zero homology for length 1 mod3. Each T supplies exactly one external irreducible U_n in selected factors, inequivalent for distinct T. The diagonal binomial coefficients are obtained by coefficient comparison to Okura’s already published all-n nonequivariant Betti polynomial (not by mere dimension-matches for a fixed n). Read the actual verify_colored_paths.py; independently enumerated all T and binomial multiplicities for m=4..16. This is a rational representation theorem, not integral or equivariant homotopy.
residual_risks: Published Okura dimension identity is used for the closed diagonal coefficient count.
Finite eigenspace tests do not prove all n; rational splitting requires 1/n and is not an integral decomposition.

evidence: Okura Theorem 1.4 gives the polynomial sphere-count coefficient used explicitly in the proof.

originality.rationale: Okura computes the nonequivariant homotopy type and its multiplicities, which are not new. The independent action by S_n on every fiber is a stronger module question: its canonical equivariant chain decomposition and multiplicity-free external-product irreducibles are not implied by published dimensions alone. Fu–Grbić and related polyhedral-product work concerns symmetries of the indexing complex rather than this path-indexed fiber permutation action. Best-of-knowledge PASS remains qualified by general polyhedral-join equivariant decomposition literature.
residual_risks: A different general equivariant polyhedral-join theorem, beyond the inspected Fu–Grbić indexing-group/polyhedral-product result, might specialize to this decomposition.
The diagonal multiplicities are not independent novel enumerations, since Okura’s formula already implies them numerically.

value.rationale: Computes complete irreducible rational homology modules for an unbounded path–clique lexicographic family, rather than ordinary ranks, with a sharp multiplicity-free property and exact fixed-point characters. Such symmetry-resolved topology is natural for automorphism actions on graph independence complexes and can be used to determine invariants under any fiber subgroup. The ingredient from Okura is confined to preexisting dimension counts.
residual_risks: Only rational modules and full fiberwise group are classified; integral lattices and path-reversal symmetry remain open.

final_claim: For m>=4,n>=2, the rational reduced homology of Ind(P_m[K_n]) as (S_n)^m-module is the multiplicity-free external sum over independent T with all link complement path lengths 0 or 2 mod3, with U_n at fibers in T, degree |T|+Σ floor((b+1)/3)-1; its diagonal S_n restriction is Σ_p (U_n^⊗p)^[binom(p+1,3(d+1)-m)binom(d+1,p)].
limitations: No claim of novelty for published nonequivariant Betti or sphere counts.
No integral splitting or path-reversal action; finite color-action checks corroborate but do not prove all m,n.
A different general equivariant polyhedral-join theorem, beyond the inspected Fu–Grbić indexing-group/polyhedral-product result, might specialize to this decomposition.
The diagonal multiplicities are not independent novel enumerations, since Okura’s formula already implies them numerically.
